role: Independent expert, production-plan.md section 5 steps 2 and 3 (blind solve, key check). Coach only; never published.
method: Each item was loaded from tools/mock/data/full-mocks.js with the pipeline loader (the vm window context scripts/explainers/build.mjs uses) and shown as served: stem and the five choices in bank order (tools/mock/full.js escapes the stem as text, draws no QR figure and does not shuffle). The extractor withheld correct, why, traps, src, stop, nights, topic, sub and d; only field names were seen.

The served page was then rendered in Chromium at http://127.0.0.1:4107/tools/mock/full.html (FULL_1, Quantitative Reasoning, the 21 batch items at their served numbers): every stem and choice set matches the loader text exactly, no item serves a figure or a structure, the calculator button is present, and the page raised no errors.

Answers, reasoning, concept, a family and a misconception for every other choice, and confidence were written to a draft and stamped (sha256 57237242d6ce980e, 2026-10-30T09:12:55Z) before any key was read; the key check then ran by exact choice text.

Every number and every distractor route was recomputed in python (permutations and combinations, the Bayes counts per 100, unit factors, ratio parts, variance, z score, slope and distance, the mixture equation, circle and triangle areas, the Pythagorean identity with the quadrant check, the Law of Cosines at 0, 60, 90, 120 and 180 degrees, compound growth, closing speed, harmonic and geometric means, combined work rate). No item serves a SMILES, so RDKit had nothing to parse.
Stem-style hits come from the build heuristics (scripts/explainers/build.mjs stemStyleHits) run on the served stems; suggested rewordings are for Thomas and are never applied.
Families come from the closed list in scripts/explainers/families.js; missType follows the family. They are suggestions for the writer, who decides.

Bank why and trap notes, and the approved pilot record for QR-2, were read only after the key check, to flag copy the writer should not lift (bankCopy) and to compare distractor routes; where that read exposed a route the blind draft missed or a better family, the change is in revisedAfterKeyCheck with the blind wording kept. Nothing in the bank was edited.

expert.concept: Order matters (first, second and third are different places), so chain the shrinking choices: a permutation, 10 x 9 x 8.
reasoning: Ask whether order matters: first, second and third are different places, so swapping two runners makes a new outcome.
Fill the three slots in turn: 10 runners can take first, 9 are left for second, 8 for third.

misconceptions.pull: Adds the runner count and the number of places (10 + 3). Counting slots multiplies; it never adds.
misconceptions.label: Added the counts

misconceptions.pull: Multiplies the 10 runners by the 3 places (10 x 3) instead of chaining 10 x 9 x 8; no single rule lands here.
misconceptions.label: Runners times places

misconceptions.pull: Counts which three runners make the top three, ignoring order (10C3 = 120). The stem records places in order, and each group of three can be ordered 3! = 6 ways: 120 x 6 = 720.
misconceptions.label: Ignored the order

misconceptions.pull: Uses 10 x 10 x 10, as if one runner could take first and second. Once a runner places, they leave the pool.
misconceptions.label: Let runners repeat

expert.concept: Conditional probability (Bayes): restrict to the students who passed, then ask what share of them studied. P(studied given passed) = P(studied and passed) / P(passed).
reasoning: Turn the percents into people: picture 100 students, 70 who study and 30 who do not.
Studiers who pass: 90 percent of 70 = 63. Non-studiers who pass: 30 percent of 30 = 9. Passers in all: 72.
The question lives inside the 72 passers: 63 of 72 studied, 63/72 = 0.875, about 88%.

misconceptions.pull: 90% is P(passed given studied), the stem's own number. The question runs the other way: given a pass, how likely is it the student studied.
misconceptions.label: Flipped the given

misconceptions.pull: Subtracts the two pass rates (90 - 30 = 60). That gap compares the groups; it is not a share of the passers.
misconceptions.label: Subtracted the rates

misconceptions.pull: 72% is P(passed), the whole denominator. Stops before asking what share of those 72 studied.
misconceptions.label: Stopped at the total

misconceptions.pull: 70% is the share of all students who study, the starting rate before the pass is known. The pass is evidence that shifts it up.
misconceptions.label: Ignored the evidence

checks.numbers: Per 100: studied and passed 0.7 x 0.9 = 63; not studied and passed 0.3 x 0.3 = 9; passed 72; 63/72 = 0.875 (about 88%). P(passed) = 0.72; 0.9 - 0.3 = 0.60; P(studied) = 0.70.

expert.concept: Convert a rate one unit at a time with factors worth 1: km to m (x 1000) on top, hours to seconds (x 3600) on the bottom. Net: divide km/h by 3.6.
reasoning: Write the rate as a fraction: 108 km over 1 hour.
Top: 108 km x 1000 = 108,000 m. Bottom: 1 hour = 3600 s.
108,000 / 3600 = 30 m/s. Shortcut: km/h divided by 3.6.

misconceptions.pull: Multiplies by 3.6 (108 x 3.6 = 388.8) instead of dividing. Meters per second is the smaller number, so the shortcut divides.

expert.concept: Variance measures spread around the mean; when every value equals the mean, every deviation is 0, so the variance is 0.
reasoning: Find the mean: all four weights are 3 g, so the mean is 3 g.
Each deviation from the mean is 3 - 3 = 0; squared, still 0.
The average of zeros is 0. No spread, no variance.

misconceptions.pull: No standard slip lands on 1; it may come from expecting a variance of at least 1, or from 4 / 4. Weak distractor.
misconceptions.label: No spread is not 1

misconceptions.pull: 3 is the mean (and every value). The question asks how far the values sit from it.
misconceptions.label: Gave the mean

misconceptions.pull: 9 is the average of the squared weights (3^2). Variance then subtracts the squared mean: 9 - 9 = 0.
misconceptions.label: Squared the value

misconceptions.pull: 12 is the total weight, 4 x 3. Spread has nothing to do with the total.

expert.concept: Distance between two points is the hypotenuse of the right triangle made by the horizontal and vertical gaps (the Pythagorean theorem).
reasoning: Draw the right triangle: horizontal gap 9 - 3 = 6, vertical gap 5 - 0 = 5.

root 61 = 7.81 (between 7 and 8, since 49 < 61 < 64).

misconceptions.label: Never squared

misconceptions.pull: 6 is only the horizontal gap. The points also differ by 5 vertically.
misconceptions.label: Horizontal gap only

misconceptions.pull: 11 is the walk along the grid lines (6 + 5). The straight line cuts the corner, so it is shorter.
misconceptions.label: Walked the grid

misconceptions.pull: 61 is the distance squared. Take the square root.

expert.concept: Shaded region = whole minus part: circle area minus triangle area. The hypotenuse is a diameter, so r = 5/2 and the circle area is 25pi/4; the right triangle area is (1/2)(3)(4) = 6.
reasoning: Name the region: inside the circle, outside the triangle, so circle area minus triangle area.
Diameter = hypotenuse = 5, so r = 2.5 and the circle area is pi x 6.25 = 25pi/4.
Triangle area: the legs are base and height, (1/2)(3)(4) = 6.
Subtract: 25pi/4 - 6, about 13.6, a positive area.

expert.concept: sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 fixes the size of sine; the quadrant fixes the sign (third quadrant: sine and cosine both negative).

Take the root: |sin| = 0.96.
Read the quadrant: in quadrant III, y is negative, so sin = -0.96.

misconceptions.pull: That is sin^2. Take the square root.
misconceptions.label: Forgot the root

misconceptions.pull: Right sign, but uses 1 - 0.28 as if sin + cos = 1. The identity squares both.
misconceptions.label: Skipped the squares

misconceptions.pull: Two slips stacked: no squares (1 - 0.28) and no minus sign. Weak distractor.
misconceptions.label: Two slips

misconceptions.pull: Right size, but positive sine belongs to quadrant II. In quadrant III both sine and cosine are negative.
misconceptions.label: Quadrant II sign

expert.concept: Law of Cosines: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos C. At 60 degrees cos C = 1/2, so the third side is shorter than the root 74 a right angle would give.
